answers.question: Please confirm the agent's tools. Reads: list the customer's orders, returning each order's number, status, total paid, payment method, and its refund or none. Writes: cancel an order by its number (answers cancelled, is rejected because the order has just shipped, or gets no answer); issue the refund for an order by its number, for the order's total to its payment method (answers the refund, pending or issued, with its amount; returns a temporary error that creates no refund; returns a refund with status failed on a terminal error; or gets no answer); create a staff follow-up task for an order with a reason (cancellation unknown, refund not issued, refund status unknown), which creates no second task for the same order and reason. Your answers say both "handoff timeout not retried" and "On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support"; I recommend the second.
answers.recommended: Yes: these four calls, and a follow-up call with no answer is sent once more; if that also gets no answer, the agent tells the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
answers.reply:
> Confirmed, with four changes:
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 2. issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.
> 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: The refund the order system returns carries an amount. What does the agent do when that amount differs from the total the customer said yes to?
answers.recommended: The agent makes no further change with the new value, tells the customer the amount the order system returned, and hands the case to staff with a follow-up task.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Proposed default: the agent cancels an order only after the customer explicitly confirms the full proposal (which order, the refund amount and where it goes); any change after confirmation voids it.

answers.question: After a cancel call with no answer, the agent re-reads the order and, if it is still placed or processing, sends the cancel once more. Nothing says what happens when that second cancel also gets no answer. What ends it?
answers.recommended: The agent sends no third cancel. It tells the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled, issues no refund, and hands the case to staff.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Q4 If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund. Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation. Shipped, report it and issue no refund. Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Three cases nobody has settled, each of which changes what the agent does. (a) The refund is asked for again after a call with no answer: does a second refund call for an order that already has a refund return that refund rather than create a second one? If not, the agent must re-read before any retry. (b) The customer asks to cancel an order that is already cancelled. (c) The call that lists the customer's orders gets no answer. Claims put to the owner: C-20, C-30, C-31.
answers.recommended: (a) Yes, a second refund call for the same order returns the existing refund. (b) The agent says the order is already cancelled and changes nothing. (c) The agent says it cannot look up the orders right now and changes nothing.
answers.reply:
> Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund.
> The agent may retry it.
> An already cancelled order: the agent reports that and changes nothing.
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled).
> Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.
